home.attentionHint: {count} assets are declared or unverified — confirm control or document how you checked.

accounts.emailsSpotlightBody: Recovery and billing paths run through email. Register each address, link login/recovery purposes on assets and identities, then explore Impact.
accounts.emailsHint: One row per address your team cares about (work inboxes, billing, recovery). Link them from asset and identity pages.

setupChecklist.title: Initial setup checklist
setupChecklist.subtitle: Work through these once your project exists — mark items as you go (saved in this browser).
setupChecklist.reviewAssetsHint: Open the verification queue and confirm control or document how you checked.
setupChecklist.identitiesHint: Names and providers correct in Accounts.
setupChecklist.linkAccessHint: From an identity or asset Access tab — who administers what.
setupChecklist.dependenciesHint: Map DNS, deploy, auth, and billing edges on this project.
setupChecklist.verifyHint: Use the verification guide — metadata only, no secrets.

graph.title: Dependency map
graph.hint: Drag nodes, scroll to zoom, pan on the background. Use expand (top-right) for fullscreen. Click arrows or nodes for detail cards.

relationHelp.depends_on: The source asset needs the target to work (ordering, DNS, upstream API, etc.).
relationHelp.hosted_on: The source runs on or inside the target (app on VPS, site on hosting).
relationHelp.deployed_from: Deploys or releases originate from the source toward the target environment.
relationHelp.authenticated_by: The source uses the target for login or tokens (OAuth client → identity).
relationHelp.stores_data_in: Persistent data for the source lives in the target (DB, bucket, registry).
relationHelp.sends_email_via: Outbound mail from the source goes through the target (SES, SMTP).
relationHelp.domain_registered_at: Domain ownership is registered with the target registrar.
relationHelp.dns_managed_by: DNS for the source is served or managed by the target.
relationHelp.verified_with: Ownership or delivery verification ties the source to the target.
relationHelp.publishes_to: The source publishes content or builds to the target.
relationHelp.billed_through: Costs for the source are invoiced via the target account.
relationHelp.recovery_depends_on: Recovery or backup of the source depends on the target.
relationHelp.other: Custom relationship — document intent in dependency notes if needed.

dependencies.confirmDelete: Remove this dependency from the map?
dependencies.confirmRemoveDescription: Only the link between these two assets is deleted. Neither asset is removed from your inventory, passwords stay in your vault, and other dependencies are unchanged. The dependency map and impact analysis will stop showing this connection; any note on the link is lost.

impact.title: Impact analysis
impact.hint: Breadth-first list from the selected asset or identity (max depth 8).
impact.empty: No dependency edges found from this starting point.

checklist.q2: If Team inbox is lost, what recovery/login paths are affected?
checklist.q2hint: Emails tab; Impact from that identity or linked assets.

checklist.q4: Which YouTube channel and which identities have admin access?
checklist.q5: Search Console property and verification method for northline.example?
checklist.q5hint: Search Console asset (billing identity); domain asset.
checklist.q6: Dependencies: registrar vs DNS vs mailbox vs AWS SES?

checklist.q7: What runs on each VPS, deploy from which repo, SSH vault ref?
checklist.q7hint: VPS + repo assets; deployed_from / hosted_on edges; vault reference.
checklist.q8: Image storage config and consuming app?
checklist.q9: Onboard another developer without sharing passwords?
checklist.q10: What to change before GitHub→Bitbucket, Namecheap→Hostinger, or OAuth account move?

verification.title: Verification in Hilko
verification.lede: Hilko never stores secrets. Verification is how you record that a human checked control or ownership — or that the item is inventory-only until you check.
verification.statusesIntro: Each asset, dependency, and role has one status. The home dashboard counts anything that is not Confirmed yet.

statusBodies.unverified: Not reviewed yet. Typical for new rows or seed/demo data.
statusBodies.declared: You listed it in inventory (wizard, CSV, manual entry) but have not confirmed control.
statusBodies.confirmed_by_human: You or someone on the team checked access, DNS, registrar, or console login and documented how.

verification.methodsIntro: When you confirm control, add a verification record: pick how you checked and optional notes (hostnames, ticket IDs, no secrets). Methods are labels for humans — not automated probes (integrations come in a later phase).

methodBodies.dns_txt: Ownership proved via a DNS TXT record (domain, SES, Google site verification, etc.).
methodBodies.html_file: HTML file uploaded to the site root or host.
methodBodies.meta_tag: Meta tag placed in site HTML.
methodBodies.cname: DNS CNAME points to a provider verification target.
methodBodies.registrar_lock: Checked registrar WHOIS, lock, or auth codes policy.
methodBodies.provider_console: Logged into vendor admin (AWS, Google, GitHub, hosting panel) and confirmed the asset exists.
methodBodies.manual_check: Other documented check (screenshot ref, runbook step, ticket) — describe in the note.
methodBodies.other: Catch-all; still add a short note.

methodExamples.provider_console: e.g. Note: SES region eu-west-1, identity verified

flowSteps.0: Open Home → verification queue or Assets → Needs confirmation.
flowSteps.2: Use “I control this” for a quick console check, or pick a method + evidence note.
flowSteps.3: Status becomes Confirmed; the dashboard count goes down.

verification.flowNote: You can also set status in Overview and save — use Confirmed only when you have actually checked.

projects.deleteConfirmLabel: Type the project name to confirm

assets.name: Asset name
assets.loginEmailHint: Address you use to sign in — not a password.

assets.typeSpecificFieldsHint: Metadata for this asset type — stored in the inventory, not in a vault.
assets.passwordManagerItemUrlHint: Deep link to the vault item (URI or HTTPS). Never paste the password here.
assets.emailPasswordManagerLink: Vault link for this login email
assets.infraLinkHint: Quick dependency: this VPS/server runs on or depends on another project asset.
assets.dependenciesHint: Direct edges involving this asset — open linked assets to walk the map.
assets.vaultRefsHint: Where humans store secrets (metadata only — never the secret itself).
assets.verificationsHint: How ownership or control was proved (e.g. DNS TXT, HTML file).
assets.verificationQueueHint: These items are not marked confirmed yet. Open each row to record evidence or confirm control.
assets.verificationCalloutBody: Record how you checked control (console login, DNS, registrar) or confirm after a quick review.
assets.verificationStatusHint: Declared = inventory only. Confirmed = you checked access or ownership.
assets.verificationConfirmedHint: Optional: add a verification record below with method + evidence so the checklist stays auditable.
assets.confirmControlHint: Adds a provider-console check and marks the asset confirmed. Add a detailed note below if needed.
assets.configHint: Non-secret settings only (client IDs, redirect URIs, env names). Secrets belong in vault references.
assets.configSensitiveToggle: Sensitive — store as vault reference only (no value here)
assets.configSensitiveRef: Sensitive value stored in vault (metadata only here).
assets.createError: Could not save the asset. Check the fields and try again.

onboarding.title: Quick setup
onboarding.subtitle: Map your first project in a few minutes. No passwords or API keys are stored.
onboarding.welcomeBody: Hilko organizes projects, tools, sign-in accounts, and how they connect. This wizard creates your first project and a starter map you can refine later.
onboarding.welcomeList1: Projects group sites, apps, or clients.
onboarding.welcomeList2: Sign-in identities are who logs in (e.g. work Google admin); assets are the things they control (repos, domains).
onboarding.welcomeList3: You can pause anytime; progress is saved automatically.
onboarding.projectHint: Use your real product or client name. You can add more projects later.
onboarding.websiteUnverified: Domain not verified yet — save without https://
onboarding.websiteHint: When you own the domain, keep https://; otherwise tick unverified until DNS is confirmed.
onboarding.toolsHint: Pick what you use today. Optional — skip if you prefer to add things manually.
onboarding.accountsHint: Who signs in to each provider? Use names you will remember in the future.
onboarding.reviewHint: We create the project, identities you listed, and optional placeholder assets. Nothing secret is stored.
onboarding.noProvidersSelected: No providers — you can add assets from the inventory later.
onboarding.errorProjectName: Enter a project name to continue.
onboarding.errorFinalize: Could not finish setup. Try again.
onboarding.assetsHint: Each provider becomes an asset row — e.g. GitHub login vs main repo are different names and types.
onboarding.connectionsHint: When the same person uses one login for a tool, link identity → asset. Suggested dependencies reuse that pairing.
onboarding.connectionsAccessHint: Creates an asset role (who can administer the resource).
onboarding.connectionsAccessEmpty: Add identities and enabled assets on previous steps to see links here.
onboarding.connectionsDepsHint: Common edges when tools share login or DNS/mail flows — adjust later on the project map.
onboarding.connectionsDepsEmpty: Pick more related providers (e.g. DNS + registrar) to see suggestions.
onboarding.reviewNextStepsHint: You land on the project with next steps — confirm assets, finish links, document dependencies, then verify.

generic.roleHint: The person or account used to sign in — not the repo or domain itself.

github.roleHint: GitHub login — distinct from the repository asset you deploy.

gitlab.roleHint: Account that signs in to GitLab — not the project URL.

google.roleHint: Workspace or Cloud sign-in — separate from OAuth client IDs on assets.

cloudflare.roleHint: Who manages DNS — the zone is the asset.

namecheap.roleHint: Registrar login vs the domain asset.

aws.roleHint: Human sign-in vs the AWS account / workload asset.

hetzner.roleHint: Console login — the server is the asset.

bitwarden.roleHint: Who unlocks the vault — references only, no secrets stored.

stripe.roleHint: Dashboard user vs the payment service asset.

vercel.roleHint: Team sign-in vs hosted app/project resource.
